NATURAL-LANGUAGE HYPOTHESIS — DiscoveryBench (archaeology)

Between 3400 BCE and 3000 BCE (Middle Neolithic, MN), and at the resolution actually sampled in the supplied regional-Z series (five 100-year bin centres), MonumentCount and AxesCelts do NOT cleanly track the supplied symbolic-capital composite (mean of HatchetSword, Dagger and HouseSize Z-scores). Over the window the targets net RISE while the composite net DECLINES; all pairwise target × composite correlations fall in the weak band (|r| < 0.5) at this N, where direction and magnitude — not p-values — carry the weight of any claim. No clean co-movement statement is therefore warranted; specifically the two targets do not converge on a single shared trajectory with the composite, so the claim is NOT generalised across them.

(i) Per-target signed change, 3400 → 3000 BCE (raw Z; older to younger):
  • MonumentCount: Z-values −0.46, −0.13, +0.91, +0.35, −0.36 at BCE 3400, 3300, 3200, 3100, 3000. Δ(3000 − 3400) = +0.10 σ; per-100-yr OLS slope = +0.069 σ. Mild net RISE; non-monotonic with a clear peak at 3200 BCE.
  • AxesCelts: +0.37, +0.32, +2.60, +0.80, +0.80. Δ = +0.43 σ; per-100-yr OLS slope = +0.134 σ. Clear net RISE, driven by a 3200 BCE spike of +2.60 σ.

(ii) Per-indicator signed change, symbolic-capital components:
  • HatchetSword: −0.43, −0.43, −0.43, −0.42, −0.43. Δ = 0.00 σ; slope = +0.001 σ/100y. Essentially CONSTANT.
  • Dagger: −0.58 in every bin. Δ = 0.00 σ; slope = 0.00 σ/100y. CONSTANT; correlation with this predictor is mathematically undefined.
  • HouseSize: +2.05, +0.79, +0.79, −0.06, +0.19. Δ = −1.86 σ; slope = −0.457 σ/100y. Strong net DECLINE — the only real within-window source of movement in the symbolic-capital composite.

(iii) Composite symbolic-capital trajectory and direction relative to each target:
  • Composite (mean of the three Zs): +0.347 → −0.073 → −0.073 → −0.353 → −0.273 (BCE 3400→3300→3200→3100→3000). Δ = −0.620 σ; slope = −0.152 σ/100y. Net DECLINE; trough at 3100 BCE with a partial recovery by 3000 BCE.
  • Relative to MonumentCount (net +0.10 σ): OPPOSITE net direction.
  • Relative to AxesCelts (net +0.43 σ): OPPOSITE net direction.
  • Per-bin sign agreement over the four 100-yr transitions of Δ(target) vs Δ(composite): AxesCelts = 2 agree, 0 oppose, 2 ties (never directly opposes), MonumentCount = 1 agree, 2 oppose, 1 tie. Bin-to-bin level: AxesCelts and the composite move compatibly whenever both move; MonumentCount is mixed. Window level: both targets and the composite go in opposite net directions.
  • Coincident feature (descriptive only): MonumentCount and AxesCelts peak SYNCHRONOUSLY at 3200 BCE — one 100-yr bin BEFORE the composite's 3100 BCE trough. This lag-of-one-bin alignment is NOT supported by a robust correlation but is visible in the trajectory plot.

(iv) Pairwise Pearson and Spearman, N=5 (touchstone: |r|≥0.7 strong; 0.5–0.7 moderate; <0.5 weak/null; magnitudes not p-values):
  Target × SymCapital (composite):
    • MonumentCount:  r = −0.351,  ρ = −0.410 — WEAK.
    • AxesCelts:      r = −0.168,  ρ = −0.368 — WEAK.
  Target × Domain components (for completeness):
    • MonumentCount × HouseSize: r = −0.352, ρ = −0.410 — WEAK.
    • AxesCelts     × HouseSize: r = −0.167, ρ = −0.368 — WEAK.
    • MonumentCount × HatchetSword: r = +0.285, ρ = +0.354 — WEAK. HatchetSword is near-constant (only a 0.01σ blip at 3100 BCE), so its apparent correlations are mechanical artefacts at N=5; not relied on.
    • AxesCelts     × HatchetSword: r = −0.106, ρ = +0.181 — WEAK, same caveat.
    • Either target × Dagger: UNDEFINED (Dagger is a constant series across all five bins).
  Auxiliary (not asked, plotted only): MonumentSize × SymCapital: r = +0.087, ρ = −0.205 — WEAK. MonumentSize × HatchetSword: r = +0.633, ρ = +0.707 — touches the moderate band but is disregarded because of the near-constant predictor.

Discretionary-band rule: neither target × composite pairing clears |r| ≥ 0.7 in either Pearson or Spearman; therefore a clean co-movement claim is NOT made. MonumentCount and AxesCelts are NOT stated to track the symbolic-capital composite cleanly, and the claim is NOT generalised across them.

Cross-encoding check (single, not duplicated in the narrative): values from capital.csv and from time_series_data.csv raw Z columns were compared at all five bin centres. Across the six comparable columns (HatchetSword, Dagger, HouseSize, MonumentCount, AxesCelts, MonumentSize) the maximum absolute difference at any node was 0.00 — they encode the same underlying 100-yr regional Z series. The narrative above is built from capital.csv.

Scope: the analysis is restricted to BCE 3400 → 3000 (inclusive), uses the raw bin-centre Z values, treats the `_inter` columns of time_series_data.csv as visualisation reference only, and does NOT extrapolate before BCE 3400 or after BCE 3000. Per the agreed scoping, the pollen-PCA openness file (Belau / Woserin, Feeser et al. 2019) is not used as evidence for the claim; it spans the window but is environmental context only.

WORKFLOW (concise):
  Load capital.csv (German locale, comma decimals) and time_series_data.csv raw Z columns; build a 5-row frame at BCE = 3400, 3300, 3200, 3100, 3000 carrying the symbolic-capital components (HatchetSword, Dagger, HouseSize), targets (MonumentCount, AxesCelts), auxiliary monument indicator (MonumentSize), and a SymCapital composite (mean of the 3 Zs); verify equivalence with time_series_data.csv at the 5 nodes (max |Δ| = 0); compute Δ(3000 − 3400) and per-100-yr OLS slopes; compute Pearson and Spearman correlations against each predictor; tabulate Δ-sign agreement per 100-yr transition; emit a 900×560 vector SVG trajectory plot of all seven series. N=5; touchstone bands (|r|≥0.7 strong, 0.5–0.7 moderate, <0.5 weak/null) drive all narrative thresholds; p-values are not used as the basis for any claim.
